concept: Data Investigation And SQL For FDEs
title: Data Investigation And SQL For FDEs Checkpoint

questions.prompt: Joining tickets to multiple shipment events inflates the ticket count. What should you inspect first?

options.label: The row grain and one-to-many relationship before aggregating.
Increase database memory until the count looks plausible.
Rename the count field to make the larger number acceptable.

questions.explanation: A correct join can multiply rows when grains differ. Resource changes and renaming do not correct the population being counted.

questions.prompt: An import contains unknown states and malformed timestamps. What preserves evidence?

options.label: Silently delete the rows and report only clean successes.
Convert every unknown state to delivered.
Quarantine invalid rows with reasons and report completeness.

questions.explanation: Quarantine and counts preserve what was excluded and why. Silent deletion hides coverage loss; invented values change business meaning.

questions.prompt: The SQL fixture must retain a ticket with no matching order. Which join shape is appropriate?

options.label: A left join on order ID alone because left joins enforce tenant permissions.
A left join on tenant and order identity, with independent caller authorization.
An inner join on order ID alone.

questions.explanation: The left join preserves unmatched tickets; the composite predicate preserves the fixture identities. Join type itself does not authorize access.

questions.prompt: A source API returns HTTP 200 but its export is ninety minutes old. What is established?

options.label: The endpoint responded; business data freshness still needs its own check.
The data must be current because HTTP succeeded.
The status must be false because old data can never be useful.

questions.explanation: Reachability and freshness are separate properties. Timestamp and workflow requirements determine whether the result is usable; neither success nor age alone proves its business truth.
